frank.summary: Historical Digital Retina is substantial reusable implementation/eval ancestry, but every visual measurement must bind exact dataset, threshold, matching rule, stage/config and tuning lineage. Map visual outputs into typed VisualPercept rather than treating captions as truth.

harness.summary: Add historical Retina strict-Freshset/threshold sweep plus art-AI/OCR/binding/hallucination fixtures; add LCME contradiction invalidation and 200-turn retention tests; bind final model receipts to exact checkpoint/config hashes.

clay.summary: Retina supports a modular multi-stage physical vision pipeline, but semantic crossing stays Clay-native and uncertainty/provenance must survive each stage. Historical weak-signal CLIP coverage cannot substitute for semantic correctness.

gwt.summary: Visual candidates require stage/source uncertainty and provenance so GWT experiments can distinguish raw availability, selection, causal use and false-evidence amplification.

emergenz.summary: Do not interpret improved multi-stage Retina coverage as emergent intelligence without ablations; Region-BLIP historical regressions show added stages can worsen output. Use lesion/rescue and interaction tests.

claycode.summary: VisualPercept contracts should encode source/frame identity, uncertainty, transform lineage and stage-derived evidence; model/vision outputs remain proposals/evidence, never authority.

claygraph.summary: Use LCME as a differential baseline and explicitly represent contradiction supersession/temporal validity; 7/10 contradiction handling is a concrete historical failure oracle.

unifieddb.summary: Store benchmark/config/provenance identity for VisualPercepts and checkpoint lineage; memory fact validity must support explicit supersession rather than relying on retrieval ranking.

q12_index.summary: Drive now exposes significant code/model/eval assets outside the 655-document concept index. Retina contributes a provisional unique 5h center mapping candidate; LCME and adapter receive zero duplicate/quality credit respectively.
